findings.message: Scope in and criterion 2 require counting re-reports 'deduped by the Box enqueue or semantic-triage path' onto a tombstoned record. Semantic-triage tombstoning happens in the triage consumer (`__main__._triage_pass` and the triage call path), not in `squatch/box.py`. Box has no hook for it: `Box.resolve` only moves a pending message to tombstoned, and `Box.enqueue` dedups only on signature. The code that must change is outside the fence.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: The reopen must append a `tombstone_auto_reopened` journal signal before the mutation. `Box` is constructed with only state_dir, fs, clock, and an optional occurrence recorder, and has no journal. For that write to happen in production, the Box composition roots (`squatch/__main__.py`, `squatch/serve.py`, drain/daemon) must pass in a journal-backed hook. None of those roots is fenced. Without them the feature is fixture-only wiring, which the ticket's own Definition of rejected forbids.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: Scope in and criterion 2 require that 'triage authors its ticket `draft` regardless of the normal class policy'. The box-triage ticket landed starting-state resolution in `squatch/policy.py`, and the author-stage ticket landed authoring in the Author stage. Neither is fenced, and the plan's retro-box-activation paragraph does not grant this override. Box can store a reopen marker, but nothing in the fence makes authoring honor it.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: The merge-time signal must carry `box_id` and `retro_report_key` from the source Box record, never inferred from the stem. Merge has no Box dependency, and no Box query by resolution link (authored stem) exists. `Box.by_origin` matches origin only. If Box has to be injected through `stages.compose`/`compose_pipeline`/`Serve`, those files are unfenced. The ticket does not say how merge reaches the Box record inside its fence.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: Criterion 1 requires exactly one `retro_finding` per proposal through the existing enqueue. But `signature()` removes digits and path tokens from `detail` and ignores `summary`. Two proposals from one report that differ only in numbers or spec paths would therefore dedup into one record.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: Binding the live hook in `squatch/__main__.py::_drain` makes every merge-then-quiesce run through `main(["drain"])` perform a FORCED retro, because no report exists yet. That adds one model request and either a main-checkout receipt commit or a `retro_failed` signal plus a `failure_report` Box message. Existing suites that drive this root assert behavior this contradicts, and none of them is in the fence. `tests/test_drain_reentry.py::test_an_always_red_verification_is_excused_and_filed_before_review` unpacks exactly one Box message with `[report] = ...`, and its scripted `Agent` has no retro answer. The same exposure applies to the other `main(["drain"])` suites: `tests/test_seed_successor.py` (exact main-history ancestry), `tests/test_drain_upgrade.py`, `tests/test_daemon_composition.py`, `tests/test_kill_cli_activation.py`, `tests/test_storm_hold.py`, `tests/test_storm_notification_activation.py`, `tests/test_restart_timers.py`, `tests/test_provider_cooldown_failover.py`, `tests/test_watchdog_activation.py`, `tests/test_daemon_pause.py`, and `tests/test_control_cli.py`.
findings.paved_road: Trace every existing test that reaches `_drain` through `main(["drain"])` and merges before quiescence. Either fence each one whose asserted Box contents, model-call sequence, journal events, or main history the forced retro changes, and name the exact assertions to migrate, or state in Scope in a mechanism allowed by the plan that keeps them unchanged, and list them as preservation-only suites run unchanged in Verification.

findings.message: Scope in says the hook renders the retro prompt and commits a receipt. But the dependencies `_drain` must supply (main repo, journal, clock, filesystem, Git/Effects, Box) include no LLM, Driver, or Stages client to make the governed `retro` call. The ticket also never says how the model output becomes the receipt. `LLMStage` requires an `emits` Artifact type, and the ticket forbids registering one in `squatch/artifacts.py` or `squatch/stages.py`. The implementer cannot tell where the model call comes from, or whether it must share the session's provider/cooldown payload.
findings.paved_road: Name the model dependency the production hook receives: for example, the existing `Driver` running an `LLMStage` named `retro` built from `specs/retro.md`, over the lock-held session's shared provider payload. State that the emitted artifact type is defined locally in `squatch/retro.py`, and that the Markdown receipt is rendered from it. Add that dependency to the `_drain` binding sentence and to the composition acceptance criterion.
